original.title: Self-efficacy: Toward a unifying theory of behavioral change.

core_idea: Self-efficacy is a person's belief in their ability to carry out the actions needed for a specific task. It shapes which tasks people choose, how much effort they put in and how long they persist. It comes from four sources: mastery experiences, vicarious experience, verbal persuasion and physiological and emotional states.

when_to_use: How do students' or employees' beliefs in their abilities relate to performance or persistence?
Which sources of self-efficacy (mastery, role models, feedback) matter in a programme?
Typical data: task-specific self-efficacy scales, interventions, interviews.
common_mistakes: Measuring general self-confidence instead of task-specific self-efficacy.
Assuming more self-efficacy is always better.
